newsitem.title: GERMANY: Berlin camel race falls foul of animal-lovers.
newsitem.headline: Berlin camel race falls foul of animal-lovers.

text.p: A German animal welfare group urged Berliners on Wednesday to boycott a camel race planned this weekend with animals supplied by the president of the United Arab Emirates, Sheikh Zaid bin Sultan al-Nahayan.

"Even though camels are generally thought to be very adaptable animals, they are used to completely different climatic and geographical conditions," the German Federation for the Protection of Animals said in a statement.
Some 25 camels were last month put through their paces by jockeys at the Hoppengarten course in Berlin, where Sunday's race -- the first such in Europe -- is to take place.
The federation said it had also asked local politicians to stay away from the race but noted that Berlin Mayor Eberhard Diepgen had given it his backing.
It said Diepgen argued that the event had a role in the promotion of German-Arab business relations and believed that it breached no regulations on the handling of animals.
Nobody at the mayor's office was available to comment.
